response.answer: First-order conditions are sufficient for optimality if convexity holds; global dynamic programming is needed for nonconvexities or complementarities.

results.title: Which is easier to learn first, greedy or dynamic programming? - Quora
results.content: Definitely greedy algorithms, which are conceptually trivial, unlike dynamic programming, which requires more insight into the problem and sophisticated strategies to actually implement correctly for non-trivial problems. Short answer: Greedy algorithms are generally easier to learn first because they rely on local, intuitive decisions and simpler proofs; dynamic programming (DP) is conceptually harder because it requires recognizing optimal substructure, overlapping subproblems, and constructing correct recurrence + memoization/tabulation.
